name.en: Fake CRA text: “you have a refund waiting, claim it here”

how.en: A text, email or chat message says it is from the Canada Revenue Agency. It offers a tax refund by Interac e-Transfer, a GST/HST credit, a Grocery Rebate or another benefit, or says you must update your account or download a notice of assessment. The link leads to a fake CRA or bank sign-in page that steals your login, banking details or SIN. The CRA does not send refunds by e-Transfer or text.

text.en: A text or email from the “CRA” says you have a refund, credit or benefit to claim.
It says you must act quickly or lose the money.
A link takes you to a fake CRA or bank sign-in page.
You are asked for your SIN, banking details or login.
CRA: You have received a tax refund of $468.32 by Interac e-Transfer. Please deposit your funds within 24 hours at: [link]
Canada Revenue Agency: You are eligible for the new Grocery Rebate. Confirm your details to receive your payment: [link]

en: A refund or benefit offered by text, or by Interac e-Transfer.
A link to sign in or “deposit” your refund.
Requests for your SIN, banking details or passport number.
A web address that isn’t on canada.ca, or pressure to act fast.
Don’t click the link. Sign in to CRA My Account by typing the address yourself.
The CRA never sends refunds by e-Transfer or text, and never asks for personal information by email or voicemail.
If unsure, call the CRA using the number on its official website.
If you entered your details, call your bank and the CRA, and report it to the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre.
